item.title: Rome to Iran, Christianity to Islam: The Bible’s Endgame Revealed — Rabbi Singer
item.description:
Iran, Islam and Israel are converging at a moment Rabbi Tovia Singer believes must be understood against the backdrop of biblical prophecy, ancient Persia, Gog and Magog and the coming of Messiah.
In this wide-ranging conversation, Rabbi Singer joins Rabbi Yitzchak Botton to examine Iran, Persia, Islam, Purim, Jewish survival and the prophetic events described in Tanakh. If the final conflict is beginning to take shape, what does Israel truly need in order to endure?
Why does Persia occupy such an important place in the biblical vision of the end times? Why does the story of Esther and Haman suddenly feel so contemporary? And must conditions become more dangerous before redemption comes?
Rabbi Singer explores passages in Jeremiah, Zechariah and Ezekiel concerning the return of the Jewish people to their land, the war of Gog and Magog and the dramatic events surrounding Israel’s ultimate redemption.
Rabbi Botton then draws a powerful parallel between ancient Persia and modern Iran, asking what the Purim story can teach the Jewish people when confronted once again by enemies seeking their destruction.
The discussion ultimately turns to a deeper question: What is Israel’s greatest source of strength?
Military power matters. Political strategy matters. But the Purim story points to something deeper.
The conversation focuses on Jewish unity, responsibility for one another and the spiritual power of becoming one people. Rabbi Botton describes that unity as a vital “secret” of Jewish survival — and perhaps one of the most important lessons for Israel as history moves toward redemption.
@RabbiYitzchakBotton @Hidabrootcom

item.title: It’s Happening Now! 5787—Daniel 12:12 | Islam, Christianity, Gog War & Messiah
item.description:
Powerful Interview! Are biblical end-time prophecies beginning to unfold before our eyes?
Rabbi Tovia Singer joins Rabbi Yitzchak Botton for a sweeping conversation about Daniel 12, Jerusalem, the Temple Mount, Christianity, Islam, Israel, the Messiah—and the prophetic journey from conflict to world peace.
At the center of the discussion is one of Daniel’s most mysterious numbers: 1,335. Why does Rabbi Singer connect the year 691 with Daniel’s 1,335 and arrive at 2026? What is the significance of Jerusalem and the Temple Mount in biblical prophecy? And what ultimately happens to the competing religious claims of Christianity, Islam, and Israel when the Messianic era arrives?
The conversation explores the history of Jerusalem, the importance of the year 691, Daniel’s 1,290 and 1,335 figures, Israel’s return to Jerusalem, the future Beit HaMikdash—the Third Temple—and the extraordinary prophecies of Isaiah and Ezekiel concerning the Messiah, the nations, and a world filled with the knowledge of Hashem.
But this raises an even larger question: if the prophets tell us that history ends with peace, what happens before we get there?
Rabbi Singer examines Isaiah’s vision of swords being beaten into plowshares, the nations streaming to Jerusalem, and a Messianic age defined not by endless war, but by the universal knowledge of G-d and world peace.
Rabbi Botton also explores what it means for the Jewish people to become a light unto the nations at a moment in history when Torah can reach billions of people across the globe.
Daniel. Jerusalem. The Temple Mount. Messiah. The nations. And the question hanging over our generation: are we watching biblical prophecy unfold? @RabbiYitzchakBotton @Hidabrootcom
